summary: Young woman with long-standing poorly controlled type 1 diabetes and multiple prior DKA episodes, now 5 weeks postpartum (infant in NICU), admitted to the ICU with severe DKA: glucose 854, HCO3 3, anion gap 36, pH 6.96, with concomitant lactic acidosis (lactate 3.6–5.4) and marked electrolyte derangement (K 8.8, Phos 7.1, Mg 7.4, transient Cr 1.4). Precipitant was medication nonadherence/running out of insulin in the setting of social stress; no infectious source identified (clear CXR, no pneumonia, negative UE ultrasound, head CT normal). She improved on insulin infusion and fluids, transferred to medicine, and pelvic ultrasound for persistent postpartum bleeding showed only intracavitary blood products without retained products of conception.
most_likely: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma, precipitated by insulin nonadherence

differential.diagnosis: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma
supporting_evidence: Glucose 854, HCO3 3, anion gap 36, pH 6.96
Chief complaint 'DKA'; treated with insulin drip and IVF
Alert/oriented x3, no coma documented
differential.reasoning: Textbook severe DKA with documented biochemical criteria and insulin-drip treatment; the condition that occasioned the ICU admission and principal focus of care.

differential.diagnosis: Severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis with lactic acidosis
supporting_evidence: Lactate 5.4 and 3.6 mmol/L, later 1.9
CXR ordered for 'unexplained lactic acidosis'
Base excess -28, calTCO2 5
opposing_evidence: Lactate cleared rapidly with volume resuscitation
differential.reasoning: Explicitly named as a problem in the hospital course and objectively supported; a codable complication of the hypoperfusion/ketoacidosis rather than a competing principal diagnosis.

supporting_evidence: K 8.8 whole blood, serum K 6.8 on admission
Later hypokalemia (K 3.0) during insulin therapy
opposing_evidence: Resolved rapidly, normal K 4.1 at discharge
differential.reasoning: Marked transcellular-shift hyperkalemia typical of severe DKA, requiring monitoring and treatment; clearly documented in labs.

differential.diagnosis: Insulin nonadherence / underdosing of prescribed insulin regimen
supporting_evidence: Admitted 'in the setting of running out of medications'
'Likely nonadherence' in hospital course; social work involved
Preadmission medication list flagged as possibly inaccurate
differential.reasoning: Documented precipitant of this DKA episode; codable as underdosing/noncompliance and relevant to recurrence risk.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury secondary to volume depletion
supporting_evidence: Creatinine 1.4 with BUN 26 on admission, baseline 0.5–0.7
Granular and hyaline casts on urinalysis
Creatinine 0.6 after fluid resuscitation
opposing_evidence: AKI not explicitly named in the hospital course text
differential.reasoning: Transient creatinine rise with rapid resolution on fluids meets prerenal AKI criteria, though documentation is only lab-based.

differential.diagnosis: Persistent postpartum vaginal bleeding without retained products of conception
supporting_evidence: 5 weeks post-partum with persistent daily vaginal bleeding
TVUS: heterogeneous endometrial material, likely blood products, no vascularity
GYN consult: normal postpartum; GYN follow-up arranged
opposing_evidence: No retained products; deemed physiologic by GYN
differential.reasoning: An active secondary problem evaluated this stay, but attributed to normal postpartum involution rather than pathology.

differential.diagnosis: Sepsis or occult infection as DKA precipitant
supporting_evidence: WBC 17.9–19.2 with 80% neutrophils; lactate 5.4
Pyuria (WBC 10/hpf, bacteria) on urinalysis
opposing_evidence: 'No infectious precipitant identified' per hospital course
Afebrile; clear chest radiographs; no antibiotics documented
differential.reasoning: Leukocytosis and lactate are explained by DKA stress response; explicit clinical statement that no infection was found lowers this substantially.

differential.diagnosis: Upper extremity deep vein thrombosis related to PICC line
supporting_evidence: RUE swelling and tenderness prompting ultrasound
Bilateral UE ecchymoses and left PICC on exam
opposing_evidence: Ultrasound showed no DVT and no soft tissue abnormality
differential.reasoning: Considered and actively excluded by duplex ultrasound; retained only as a documented rule-out.

rule_outs.why: Transvaginal ultrasound showed only avascular endometrial blood products; GYN judged normal postpartum findings.
Duplex ultrasound demonstrated patent, compressible veins with no thrombus or soft tissue abnormality.
Serial chest radiographs clear with no consolidation, effusion, or congestion despite lactic acidosis.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Acute intracranial process causing altered mental status
rule_outs.why: Noncontrast head CT showed no hemorrhage, infarct, edema, or mass; mentation normalized with DKA correction.
Pyuria present but no fever, no documented culture-proven infection, and course states no infectious precipitant.

uncertain_areas: Whether urine/blood cultures were positive would elevate an infectious precipitant and possibly sepsis coding
Whether AKI was formally documented by the treating team affects secondary diagnosis capture
Exact postpartum interval and whether obstetric puerperal codes (O24.03) apply given delivery ~5 weeks prior
Whether hypernatremia (Na 148), hypomagnesemia/hypermagnesemia, and hypophosphatemia were treated as separate problems
Confirmation of altered mental status severity (would distinguish DKA with vs. without coma)
